title: Cohomology vanishing is detected on a finite standard-open cover
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $M^\bullet$ a complex of $A$-modules, and $f:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\to A$ a finite family generating the unit ideal. View its cohomology in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and localize termwise at each $f_i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For any integer $n$, if $H^n(M^\bullet\otimes_A A_{f_i})=0$ for every $i$, then $H^n(M^\bullet)=0$.

source.place: Tag 066D, proof, first paragraph; Algebra, Tag 00EO (1)

proof.text: Construct the private tensorEquiv by tensor-product lifts in both directions, sending s tensor x to the same pure tensor for the restricted scalar action. The maps are inverse by induction on tensors. This is ModuleCat.tensorEquivExtendScalars with the module universe generalized; no object is chosen from an existence assertion.

For each i, A localized away from f_i is flat (IsLocalization.flat). Module.Flat.lTensor_exact preserves exact pairs. Transport this exactness through tensorEquiv, whose naturality follows by induction on tensors, to show termwise extension of scalars preserves every exact short complex. Functor.exact_tfae gives preservation of homology.

Compose DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors with Functor.mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso from the proved source-library module WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.PreservesQuasiIso. The local hypothesis therefore says that extension of scalars of M.homology n is a zero object. These are the canonical homology comparison isomorphisms for exact functors.

For x in M.homology n and a in the range of f, choose an index i with f_i=a. tensorEquiv carries 1 tensor x into a zero module, so injectivity shows 1 tensor x=0. The localization/base-change instance makes TensorProduct.mk A (Localization.Away a) H 1 a module localization. Apply Module.eq_zero_of_isLocalized_span to Set.range f and hf. Every x is zero, so H is a zero object. Transfer back by homologyFunctorFactors. This includes the empty family, since the Mathlib zero criterion requires only span(range f)=top.

lean.statement:
theorem homology_vanishes_of_localization_span
    {A : Type u₁} [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} A)]
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} A) ℤ)
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    [∀ i : Fin r, HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} (Localization.Away (f i)))]
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (n : ℤ)
    (hlocal : ∀ i : Fin r,
      IsZero ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} (Localization.Away (f i))) n).obj
        (Q.obj ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f i))))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M)))) :
    IsZero ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} A) n).obj (Q.obj M))
